title: Random Input
opening: An arbitrary input can interrupt a familiar filter. Its properties may suggest a connection; the connection still has to fit the actual task.

example.heading: Generate first. Evaluate second.
example.context: A hypothetical teacher wants a short exercise that helps someone move from stating a definition to applying it to a new case. This is an example need, not a report about a real learner.

options.connection: Add one worked step between the definition and the new case.
options.fit: This could fit if the missing move is the transition from knowing the definition to using it.
options.limit: If the learner does not know which feature matters, a transition step alone may miss the issue.
options.check: Ask the learner to name the definition, identify the relevant feature in a case, and apply it. Which move is missing?

options.property: Makes nearby details easier to see.
options.connection: Mark the feature to notice in each new case.
options.fit: This could fit if the missing move is noticing which feature of the case matters.
options.limit: If the learner identifies the feature but cannot use the definition, more highlighting may not bridge that step.
options.check: Ask the learner to point to the feature that changes the case, then explain how the definition applies. Which move is missing?

example.boundary: Neither object proves what a learner needs. The observed task and a small check can change which candidate is worth exploring.

practice.question: A current question or task I want another angle on
practice.input: An arbitrary word or object (you may use the local draw button)
practice.property: One concrete property or relation of that input
practice.connection: A candidate connection to the actual task
practice.evaluation: What purpose or constraint could it fit? What limit or small check would change your view?

labels.comparison: Two possible connections for one hypothetical teaching need
labels.sourceQuote: Random Input: take an arbitrary word, image or object and use its properties to generate a new connection.
labels.practiceHeading: Try one on your own question
labels.practiceIntro: Keep the arbitrary input, its property and the proposed connection separate. A surprising idea is only a candidate. Partial drafts are useful, and you do not need to act on or share the idea.
labels.privacy: Your writing is saved as private lesson practice. Saving does not grade the idea or mark the lesson complete.
labels.drawHelp: A local draw chooses from a short word list; you can replace it or enter another object.
